requirements.title: Add universal engineering ruleset
requirements.description: Create the controlling OmniContext engineering ruleset and align the workspace instructions to it.
acceptance_criteria: The global ruleset exists as a framework-agnostic source of truth.
Assistant entrypoint shims point to the .ai entrypoint sources.
Completion workflow requires validation, documentation, changelog, and reporting.
risk_notes: Project-specific placeholders must be filled before use in a target repository.

requirements.title: Create OmniContext README and visual
requirements.description: Build the public-facing README around OmniContext and include an architecture diagram.
acceptance_criteria: README explains the OmniContext problem, pattern, setup, daily use, and validation workflow.
README includes an SVG architecture diagram.
Changelog records the documentation update.
risk_notes: License text remains project-specific and should be filled before publication.

requirements.title: Add OmniContext doctor and requirement registry
requirements.description: Make the workspace more powerful by adding a dependency-free CLI doctor, requirement registry, and schema-backed validation documents.
acceptance_criteria: CLI supports sync, doctor, and validate commands.
Doctor validates required files, JSON parsing, ruleset keys, requirements structure, assistant pointer drift, README architecture reference, and changelog presence.
Requirements registry tracks completed project requirements.
README documents the new CLI workflow.
risk_notes: Doctor currently implements lightweight schema checks with the Python standard library rather than a full JSON Schema engine.

requirements.title: Centralize fallback rules for LLM entrypoints
requirements.description: Add explicit fallback operating rules for assistant entrypoints in case an assistant skips or cannot follow the primary .ai configuration.
acceptance_criteria: A shared fallback contract exists inside .ai/entrypoints.
A structured fallback rulepack exists inside .ai/rules.
All assistant entrypoint shims point to .ai entrypoint sources and the centralized fallback contract.
The sync command regenerates .ai entrypoint sources and assistant shims.
The sync command skips existing non-Omni files unless --force is used.
Doctor validates the fallback contract and fallback rulepack as required source-of-truth files.
README and changelog document the fallback behavior.
risk_notes: Fallback rules intentionally duplicate core constraints in a centralized fallback contract to reduce skipped-context risk without bloating root shims.

requirements.title: Clarify OmniContext purpose and make_ai role
requirements.description: Update README positioning to explain the unique context-drift use case and clarify that make_ai.py is optional maintenance tooling, not required for normal cloned-repo usage.
acceptance_criteria: README explains OmniContext as a repo-local control plane for AI coding assistants.
README explicitly states the unique problem is AI context drift across tools.
README explains that cloned repositories do not require make_ai.py for normal usage.
make_ai.py help text describes the script as maintenance tooling.
Changelog records the documentation clarification.
risk_notes: Clarification avoids presenting the maintenance script as mandatory setup for users who clone a complete repository.

requirements.title: Replace Python data rules with data governance rules
requirements.description: Rename the Python-specific data rule file and refocus it on bounded, framework-agnostic data governance.
acceptance_criteria: Python-specific data rules are removed from the universal ruleset surface.
A data-governance rule file covers data boundaries, contracts, validation, transformations, privacy, persistence, migrations, and testing.
Doctor validates the renamed rule file as required.
README references the new data governance rule name.
Changelog records the ruleset refinement.
risk_notes: The rule is intentionally bounded to data behavior and avoids language-specific implementation guidance.

requirements.title: Convert enforceable rule files to JSON
requirements.description: Replace Markdown rule implementations with schema-backed JSON rulepacks so doctor can validate rule IDs, severities, scopes, and statements.
acceptance_criteria: Enforceable companion rule files are represented as JSON rulepacks.
Old Markdown rule implementation files are removed from .ai/rules.
Each JSON rulepack contains stable rule IDs, severities, scopes, and statements.
A rulepack schema documents the structured rule format.
Doctor validates structured rulepacks.
README documents JSON rulepacks instead of Markdown rule implementations.
risk_notes: Markdown remains appropriate for README and core human-facing overview files; enforceable policy is now JSON.

requirements.title: Add low-friction rule and requirement editing
requirements.description: Create an easy CLI interface for adding requirements and rulepack rules without manually editing long JSON files.
acceptance_criteria: CLI can add requirements with defaults
CLI can add rules to rulepacks with defaults
README documents the authoring interface
Doctor validates the resulting JSON
risk_notes: CLI intentionally stays lightweight and flag-based to avoid adding dependencies

requirements.title: Add omni command entrypoint
requirements.description: Provide an easy omni command so users can run omni doctor and omni sync instead of python3 make_ai.py doctor and python3 make_ai.py sync.
acceptance_criteria: Repo-local ./omni command works
Editable install can expose an optional omni console script
Doctor validates the repo-local command entrypoint and warns, rather than fails, when the optional console script is absent
README documents omni doctor and omni sync
Fallback instructions use omni commands
risk_notes: Exact omni command without ./ requires installing the package or adding the repo root to PATH; existing projects do not need to modify pyproject.toml to use ./omni

requirements.title: Remove tomllib dependency
requirements.description: Remove the Python 3.11-only tomllib import so editors using Python 3.10 do not report unresolved imports.
acceptance_criteria: make_ai.py has no tomllib import
Doctor treats the pyproject console script as optional
Package metadata supports Python 3.10 or newer
Validation passes
risk_notes: pyproject validation is intentionally lightweight and checks the expected console script line rather than fully parsing TOML
